items.evidence: With no engine running, `python tools/kit_check.py build` (from work/) started a windowless engine, built all four recipes, stopped it, exit 0, and printed a JSON list of name/triangles/closed/bounds: gear_token 320 true, heart 2300 true, star 36 true, coin 576 true, with x/y/z min-max for each.

`python tools/kit_check.py frames` rewrote frames/gear_token.png, heart.png, star.png and coin.png (timestamps 20:09). The PNG headers read 512x512. I opened all four: each is a front view with the whole prop centred and margin on every side.

The gear frame shows 12 equal teeth and a round hole with the background showing through. In the exported gear_token.glb the front-face tip vertices form 12 clusters centred at 0,30,...,330 deg, each 7.5 deg wide and spaced exactly 30 deg apart. The hole vertices are all at r=0.03 (32 of them), and no triangle covers the centre in XY projection.
Headless build bounds for gear_token: x -0.15..0.15 (0.30), y 0..0.30 (0.30), z -0.025..0.025 (0.05). All are within 5% and it stands on y=0.

The frame reads clearly as a heart, with two lobes on top and a point down. The edges are not rounded, though. heart.glb has a flat back cap at z=-0.025 (62 tris, nz=-1) and a flat front cap at z=0.025 (62 tris, nz=+1). The 18 vertex rings between them all sit within 0.1 mm of the outline (xmax 0.15000 at z=-0.025 vs 0.14990 at z=0.025), and 2048 of the 2300 triangles have nz=0. So the side is a vertical wall meeting both caps at a right angle: the 'pillow' raise used inset 0.0001, so it never domes.

The star frame shows five sharp points with one up. In star.glb the outer vertices are at r=0.1577 and angles 18,90,162,234,306 deg (72 deg apart), with inner vertices at r=0.0602, so each point is a single sharp vertex. Bounds are x -0.15..0.15 (0.30 across), y 0..0.285 and z +-0.025 (0.05 thick).

Coin bounds are x +-0.1 (0.2 across), y 0..0.2 and z +-0.01. In coin.glb the rim between r=0.085 and r=0.1 spans z +-0.01 on both faces, while the core at r<0.085 spans only z +-0.005, so the middle is thinner than the rim. The frame shows the rim as a ring.

The headless build reports closed=true for all four. All four recipes use the `painted` material with a colour from the one assets/style.json palette (steel, heart_red, star_yellow, gold), all are upright flat slabs, and the four frames share one flat-coloured look.

README gives `python tools/kit_check.py build` and `python tools/kit_check.py frames`. Each run from work/ with no engine running (engine_info said no_engine before), worked without help, and left no engine running (engine_info said no_engine after).

defects: Heart: the recipe's pillow raise uses inset 0.0001, so the 'rounded' rim is a straight vertical wall with square edges on front and back. README's 'gentle dome ... rim is soft' describes something the mesh does not have.
assets/style.json promises 'soft bevel on every rim' and 'a warm metal for the gear and coin', but no prop is bevelled and the gear and coin use `painted`, not `metal`.
Closedness is measured by the builder's own script on the exported .glb, not by the engine's model_build closed flag that the brief names (README says so).
Every frames run leaves another run folder of PNG/JSON files under work/captures, and these accumulate.
